questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had not been to Vienna before but always wanted to go. The University of Vienna also had interesting courses for me to attend.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The semester in Vienna overlapped with my semester in Copenhagen, which was a bit stressful.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the necessary information for incoming exchange students at the University of Vienna. Most information could be found of the webpage of International Office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found my apartment on Airbnb, but student accommodation was possible to find. I was a bit late for registration on waiting lists for dormitories, so I ended up with an Airbnb - but that was really nice as well.
I would recommend to check housing possibilities in Vienna as soon as possible in your planning.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is fairly easy to travel around Vienna either by public transport or by bike. So you do not have to live in walking distance from the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to register for exams in lecture-courses (that is very important to remember).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses and exams in the online platform U:Find. It is very simple and easy to use. You can chose between different kinds of course; either seminars and lecture series. They are graded differently and the exams  are different as well. You can read about grading, exams, and expectations in the course description on U:Find as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always contact the International Office or the Erasmus coordinators at your institute. They can be a great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the courses I wanted. Remember to check the dates and times for your chosen courses, as they can overlap. Also check the webpage of the International Office for information about course registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check dates, times, and exams for your courses! You must register for exams for lecture-series courses separately. Furthermore, I would recommend choosing a mix of seminar and lecture-series courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I attended mostly Master-courses, which was not a problem. The academic level is very dependent on the specific course instructor as they choose the reading and lead the discussion. I did not feel a big difference between the level of BA-courses and Master-courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar to UCPH with regard to both seminars (student presentations and so forth) and lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in history then I would strongly recommend any course with John Giebfried. He is one of the best instructors I have ever had making class interesting, fun, and entertaining.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The price of groceries and the prices at restaurants/bars were pretty much the same as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Student Network facilitated a lot of activities. I attended some in the beginning but not all, however I played handball at the University Sports Institute which was super great! I can highly recommend playing at the Sports Institute as you meet other students from other universities as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Playing a sport at the Univeristy Sports Institute - it is for all students in Vienna not just for students at Universiat Wien. It was a great way to meet new people and friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is easy to travel to other parts of Europe by bus from Vienna. Weekend trips into Europe or the Alps were super nice! You can also hike in the hills surrounding Vienna. That is super nice if the weather allows it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture was very similar to Copenhagen, but people from Vienna can be very annoyed in traffic - that is just how it is.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend some of the events made by the Erasmus Student Network in the start of your semester - everybody wants to meet other exchange students, so it is very easy to socialize with new people at the ESN-events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People being angry and annoyed in traffic - a lot of honking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The café-culture was super nice. Always great to grab a cup of tea after a long day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to register for exams in your lecture-courses!
Enjoy the beautiful city - explore the museums and the concert halls.
Use Vienna as a starting point for weekend trips to other parts of Europe.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You do not need to speak German to live in the city - almost everyone speaks decent English.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting wonderful friends from all over Europe. The academic leaning was nice - but the people were the best!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The end of my semester in Vienna overlapped with the beginning of my semester in Copenhagen. That was stressful but I was aware of the overlap in good time so I could plan my exams well in advance. It was nonetheless stressful.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Universität Wien is a fantastic place to study and Vienna is wonderful.  I can only recommend it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
